preamble: 29 was a recent guest on Desert Island Discs. This crossword reflects his musical choices.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Young girl by the French border's little town

parts.note: Beth is a girl's name, short for Elizabeth
le is the French masculine word for 'the'
a hem is the folded border of a garment; the 's is just a possessive

explanation.surface: A girl from a small French frontier town is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the carol 'O little town of Bethlehem'.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol famously calls the birthplace of Jesus a 'little town', so the phrase points straight to it.

clue.text: Czech region without motorway and tea

indicators.note: without means the motorway's letters are taken out of the region's name

parts.note: Bohemia is the western region of the Czech Republic
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written here as MI

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses a Czech region on back roads and stops for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London to Leeds motorway; crosswords write the figure 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohea is a black Chinese tea, once the general name for the finest black teas.

clue.text: Meddler right off Finland's third city

indicators.note: off means the letter for right is dropped from the meddler

parts.note: a tamperer is someone who meddles or interferes

explanation.surface: A busybody gets sent away from a Finnish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampere is Finland's third-largest urban centre after Helsinki and Espoo.

clue.text: Stan and knighted actor at bay

parts.note: Stan Laurel, the comic partner of Oliver Hardy
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree, the Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: Two comic and stage actors are pictured, cornered at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at bay' reads as being cornered; 'at' is only a link and 'bay' is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay tree is another name for the laurel, whose leaves are used in cooking and garlands.

clue.text: Having no capital, English had wandered in Scottish mountains

indicators.note: wandered means the remaining letters roam into a new order
having no capital means the word English loses its first letter

explanation.surface: An English traveller without money wanders through the Scottish mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having no capital' looks like being broke, but it drops the E of English; 'wandered' rearranges NGLISH plus HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highlands are the mountainous north and west of Scotland.

indicators.note: swallowing means the worker takes the company inside him

parts.note: a man is a worker, as in a hired hand

explanation.surface: An employee gulps down the firm's wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Macon is a Burgundy wine named after the town of Macon.

indicators.note: made of says the letters given are worked into something new

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A cleaning tool improvised out of a piano string.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiper, such as a windscreen wiper, is something that cleans by wiping.

clue.text: Chosen by 29, worker tucked into canapés served before farewell

indicators.note: before puts the rearranged part ahead of the farewell
tucked into means the worker is placed inside the rearranged snack letters
served suggests the canapes are dished up in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker
ta-ta is an informal British way of saying goodbye

explanation.surface: A labourer eats party snacks at a send-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' rearranges the snacks into PEASC, which 'tucked into' opens after PEAS. 29 is CINEPHILE, the compiler John Graham, whose Desert Island Discs choices supply the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Bach's Peasant Cantata was among the records this compiler picked on the radio programme.

clue.text: Inclination to study one's inner points

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: inner says the points sit inside one's

parts.note: one is I, and the 's adds S
N, E and S are compass points

explanation.surface: A tendency to study a person's innermost views.
explanation.definitionFit: Readiness means willingness or inclination to do something.

definitions.meaning: a stiff felt hat with a dented crown and curled brim
Procol Harum's song of that name was one of the compiler's records

explanation.definitionFit: The hat is named after the German spa town, and the Procol Harum song shares the name.

definitions.meaning: the pen name of the short-story writer H H Munro
the compiler chose a book by this writer

explanation.surface: A primate and a writer were both picked by the guest.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a South American monkey and was the pen name of H H Munro, the short-story writer.

clue.text: Fish and bird with new tail — nonsense

parts.note: a cod is a fish

indicators.note: with new tail means the bird's last letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a swallow is a bird

explanation.surface: A fish and a bird with a replacement tail make a ridiculous creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with new tail' changes the final W of SWALLOW to P.
explanation.definitionFit: Codswallop is British slang for rubbish or nonsense talk.

clue.text: Modify reports about support getting withdrawn

indicators.note: getting withdrawn means the whole construction is pulled back and read backwards
about means the reports surround the support

parts.note: news is reports of events
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A request to edit reports about funding that has been pulled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives NETEEWS, which 'getting withdrawn' turns around; 'Modify' fits because sweetening a deal alters its terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweeten something is to soften or alter it to make it more acceptable.

clue.text: Chosen by 29, Holtby whistled our new variations

indicators.note: variations, as in music, means the letters are played in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone called Holtby whistles new variations on a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram covers all twenty letters of HOLTBY WHISTLED OUR NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk song 'Blow the Wind Southerly', made famous by Kathleen Ferrier, was among the compiler's picks.

definitions.meaning: the letter V is in ... place in the composer's name

explanation.walkthrough: The two lights read BEETHOVEN and SEVENTH; the first S of the second light doubles as the possessive. V is not the Roman five but the seventh letter of BEETHOVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The symphony is the composer's seventh, and V sits seventh in his name, so both senses fit.

indicators.note: revealing means the low tide uncovers a run of letters within the words

explanation.surface: A falling tide uncovers a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England.

clue.text: Overcoats left by broken rest in the States

indicators.note: in says the left and broken rest go within the States

parts.note: US is the United States

indicators.note: broken means the word rest is shattered into another order

explanation.surface: Coats are left behind after an interrupted rest in America.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long loose overcoat, originally made in Ulster.

indicators.note: in means the acting letter goes within the compounds

parts.note: esters are chemical compounds formed from an acid and an alcohol
A is an abbreviation for acting, as in an acting post

explanation.surface: American residents perform in chemical compounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Easters is an American term for people living in the eastern part of a state or region.

clue.text: Old professors — ie retired and retaining worth

indicators.note: retaining says the reversed letters hold the worth inside them
retired means the abbreviation ie is turned back to front

parts.note: merit is worth

explanation.surface: Elderly academics, now retired, still keep their value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns IE into EI, which holds MERIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti are professors who have retired but keep an honorary title.

definitions.meaning: a ship '... into view', the old past tense of heave
the seaside town next to Brighton on the Sussex coast

explanation.surface: Something appeared on the horizon close to Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: Hove is the old past tense of heave in 'hove into view', and also the town beside Brighton, a seaside resort south of London.

clue.text: Sky associate in there, counting on 29's choice

indicators.note: in means the sky and associate are placed inside the word there

parts.note: taken as written and split open
the heavens are the sky
A is an abbreviation for associate, as in professional titles
telling is an old word for counting, as in a bank teller or telling votes

explanation.surface: A Sky TV associate is relying on a guest's choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky' looks like the broadcaster but is the definition-free piece; the chorus from Haydn's Creation was a choice of 29, the compiler Cinephile.
explanation.definitionFit: The chorus 'The Heavens Are Telling' from Haydn's Creation was among the compiler's selections.

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A modern part of the song White Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-tec is a spelling of hi-tech, using advanced technology, so up to date.

clue.text: Vegetable religious leader cut in half

indicators.note: cut in half means the leader's name loses its second half

parts.note: Emanuel Swedenborg, the Swedish mystic whose followers founded a church

explanation.surface: A religious figure gets chopped up like a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: SWEDENBORG has ten letters; halving leaves the first five.
explanation.definitionFit: A swede is a root vegetable, the yellow turnip or rutabaga.

parts.note: a sum is a total
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Complete devotion to wrestling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the Japanese style of wrestling between very heavy men.

indicators.note: out of says the gear word is knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A car being taken out of neutral gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Renault is a French make of car.

parts.note: a quintet is five, the Roman numeral V

indicators.note: criminal suggests the line-up is crooked and jumbled

explanation.surface: Five crafty suspects stand in a police line-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulpine means fox-like, and the fox is proverbially sly, hence crafty.

definitions.meaning: a coarse brutish person, from the brutes in Gulliver's Travels
a wild slog in cricket that goes wrong

explanation.surface: A hooligan plays a poor shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a boor, after Swift's brutish creatures, and in cricket a reckless swipe.

clue.text: Compiler's popular recording in the country

indicators.note: in means popular and recording go inside the country

parts.note: Chile is a South American country
in means popular or fashionable
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A setter's hit record is released abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Cinephile was the FT pseudonym of John Graham, better known as Araucaria in the Guardian.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the pseudonym used by a crossword setter in the Financial Times, so it names a compiler.
